lessons: Avoid starting with declarative descriptive facts about tree biology; the maple syrup video lost 38.5% of viewers at 13% duration when explaining sap composition, compared to much better retention on psychological or body-related hooks.
Do not use explicit interactive pauses asking the audience to guess; the maple syrup video suffered a 15.4% drop right after the line 'Pause and guess...'.

Hook lines that immediately establish a relatable human sensation or counterintuitive mystery (like spicy food relief failing) maintain better performance at the 50% mark (47.95%) despite poor starts.
Not enough data to conclusively determine the effect of countdowns, as all provided entries have countdown set to null.
To improve start performance relative to similar YouTube videos (currently ranging from 0.27 to 0.46), shift away from slow scene-setting sentences and lead directly with the core paradox or problem.
worst_moment_types: Explanatory scientific details delivered too early (e.g., sap water percentages at 13% video length)
Direct calls to pause and guess mid-video
best_hook_types: Not enough data to isolate specific winning hook line structures, though body/food-related mysteries perform moderately better at mid-video retention
